edits.old: DNS egress policies can break NodeLocal resolution. Inspect the actual resolver path and permit its TCP/UDP DNS traffic; a namespace-only selector failed in Argo CD’s historical GKE incident. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Network policies can break NodeLocal DNSCache resolution. On GKE clusters that use network policy with NodeLocal DNSCache and use neither Cloud DNS nor GKE Dataplane V2, you must configure rules that permit workloads and the node-local-dns Pods to send DNS queries, including TCP and UDP port 53 (Google's example uses an ipBlock for the kube-dns Service ClusterIP). Sources: https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/nodelocal-dns-cache

edits.old: Signicat’s December 2023 report described a hard-coded 20-child dnsmasq limit in its GKE NodeLocal-to-kube-dns stack. Google’s GKE documentation distinguishes legacy kube-dns through version 1.35 from CoreDNS-based kube-dns in version 1.36 and later, so Signicat’s historical observation is not a universal current GKE limit. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

edits.rationale: Signicat's blog post (dated Dec 14, 2023 in the pinned page) says dnsmasq has a hard-coded limit of 20 child processes in its GKE node-local-dns/kube-dns setup. Google's kube-dns doc separates legacy kube-dns (GKE 1.35 and earlier) from CoreDNS-based kube-dns (1.36 and later), so the Signicat observation is historical and not a universal current limit.
